headlines.title: American Express’s Q3 earnings call: our top 5 analyst questions
headlines.summary: American Express delivered revenue broadly in line with Wall Street expectations and a GAAP profit that exceeded consensus in the third quarter. Management attributed the quarter’s performance to continued strength in its premium cardmember base, robust travel and entertainment spending, and higher net card fees.

headlines.title: American Express adds $250 Airbnb credit, but there's a catch
headlines.summary: American Express is expanding its travel rewards, but Platinum cardholders should read the fine print.

headlines.title: American Express (AXP) Stock Price Drops After Strong Q3 Earnings
headlines.summary: American Express came into this Q3 2026 print with its stock near record territory and a reputation as the premium spend machine in consumer finance. The headline this quarter is simple. Revenue reached about US$19.8b and basic earnings per share landed near US$5.52, yet the share price dropped 3.7% on the day to US$313.22. That gap between stronger profit power and a sliding share price is the real story.

headlines.title: American Express Stock Shocks Despite Positive Revenue and Earnings
headlines.summary: American Express stock fell 3.62% after Q3 earnings, as a one-time gain drove most of its raised 2026 profit forecast.

headlines.title: AmEx Raised Its Profit Forecast and Announced Layoffs on the Same Day
headlines.summary: American Express beat earnings expectations and lifted its profit forecast, then disclosed plans to eliminate thousands of jobs on the same call. What spooked investors had less to do with the cuts themselves and more to do with what the company quietly left out.

description: American Express Company, together with its subsidiaries, operates as an integrated payments company in the United States, Europe, the Middle East and Africa, the Asia Pacific, Australia, New Zealand, Latin America, Canada, the Caribbean, and internationally. It operates through four segments: U.S. Consumer Services, Commercial Services, International Card Services, and Global Merchant and Network Services. The company offers credit and charge cards and complementary products and services, including travel, dining, and lifestyle and expense management products and services; and banking and other payment and financing products and services, including deposits and non-card lending. It also provides merchant acquisition and processing, servicing and settlement, fraud prevention, and point-of-sale marketing and information products and services, as well as network services. The company offers its products and services to consumers, small businesses, mid-sized companies, and large corporations through mobile and online applications, affiliate marketing, customer referral programs, third-party service providers and business partners, in-house sales teams, direct mail, telephone, and direct response advertising. American Express Company was founded in 1850 and is headquartered in New York, New York.
